title: Extreme Thrombocytosis in Patients With Malignancy; Complications, Management and Outcomes

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Extreme Thrombocytosis in Patients With Malignancy; Complications, Management and Outcomes》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Background · jha270425-sec-0060-p1】Thrombocytosis is a frequently encountered haematological abnormality. However, extreme thrombocytosis (EXT), as defined by a platelet count of > 1000 × 109/L, is a rare entity. The aetiology of thrombocytosis can be classified as either primary (i.e., clonal thrombocytosis related to an underlying myeloproliferative neoplasm [MPN]) or secondary/reactive. There are limited data on the aetiology of EXT [1]. Historically, the majority of patients with EXT were assumed to have MPN. However, subsequent studies have demonstrated that as few as 10%–15% of cases of EXT are attributable to underlying MPN [2].

【Background · jha270425-sec-0060-p2】Malignancy is a known pro‐inflammatory state, but the exact pathophysiology of EXT in malignancy is complex and likely multifactorial, involving tumour‐mediated cytokine production (with IL‐6, IL‐1, and IL‐11 implicated), bone marrow stimulation and, in some cases, contributory processes such as infection or iron deficiency [2]. The clinical significance and prognostic implications of EXT in cancer patients remain unclear with little published evidence in this area. There are also limited data regarding the management of EXT in cancer patients. It is recognised that patients with EXT are at higher risk of both thrombotic and haemorrhagic complications [3]. For this reason, risk assessment is particularly important in this cohort as they have other risk factors for these complications (i.e., active malignancy, intercurrent infection and frequent admissions to hospital) [4].

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Extreme Thrombocytosis in Patients With Malignancy; Complications, Management and Outcomes》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Methods · jha270425-sec-0070-p1】We conducted a retrospective analysis of 220 patients with at least one documented occurrence of EXT at a dedicated cancer hospital (The Royal Marsden) over a 12‐year period (January 2010 to December 2022). We used a platelet count threshold of > 1000 × 109/L based on the widely used and accepted definition of EXT in the published literature. Patients were identified by an electronic search of laboratory records, and clinical data was collected regarding patient characteristics, underlying malignancy, investigations for thrombocytosis, thrombotic complications, management and outcomes. Patients with EXT who had either a new diagnosis of or prior history of MPN were excluded from analysis (n = 22).

【Methods · abstract-2-1】Two-hundred and twenty patients with malignancy experienced at least one episode of EXT during the study period. Patients with a known or subsequent diagnosis of myeloproliferative neoplasm (MPN) were excluded from analysis. Clinical data were collected from electronic patient records.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Extreme Thrombocytosis in Patients With Malignancy; Complications, Management and Outcomes》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · jha270425-sec-0080-p1】One hundred and ninety‐eight patients were included in analysis. In terms of baseline characteristics, 113 patients were female (57%) and the median age at diagnosis of malignancy was 55 years (range 1–86). Most patients had non‐haematological malignancies (153, 77%). Of these, the most common diagnoses were lung cancer (39, 25%), pancreatic cancer (19, 12%) and bladder cancer (16, 10%). Haematological malignancy (non‐MPN) was the primary diagnosis in 45 patients (23%), the most common of which was Burkitt Lymphoma (12, 26%). Other cancer subtypes seen are outlined in Table 1.

【Results · jha270425-sec-0080-p2】The median highest platelet count reported in this patient population was 1112 × 109/L (range 1001–2593). MPN screening (JAK2, MPL, CALR and BCR‐ABL testing) was not done in the vast majority of patients; only 11 patients (5.5%) were tested.
